claims.text: Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance and undergoes rapid oxidation beyond acceptable limits.
A 1–2 μm aluminide coating can be applied to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr by controlled physical vapor deposition.
The aluminide coating will form a continuous, adherent Al2O3 surface scale during high-temperature exposure.
The aluminide coating will oxidize preferentially to form Al2O3.
The resulting Al2O3 layer will limit oxygen ingress into the underlying HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
Limiting oxygen ingress will minimize deleterious internal oxidation.
The surface-confined oxidation process will preserve the original bulk mechanical properties.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, coated specimens will have lower oxidation weight gain than untreated specimens.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, coated specimens will have a thinner and more uniform oxide scale than untreated specimens.
The aluminide coating will not detrimentally affect room-temperature tensile ductility.
The aluminide coating will not detrimentally affect tensile ductility or yield strength at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The proposed oxidation protection is applicable only up to approximately 800 °C in air for exposures around 5 hours and under low mechanical strain rates.
Higher temperatures, longer exposures, or different stress states may require alternative oxidation-protection strategies.
